_comment: Three tiles, and the point of the third is CONCURRENCY, not coverage. The shipped two-tile cut holds both EfficientNet-b0 encoders in one graph, so they serialise inside a single dispatch on one lane. They do not consume each other's output -- the goal encoder takes goal_img plus obs_img, the obs encoder takes obs_img -- so branch-mode slicing (backward closure of each compress projection) makes them independent tiles with depends_on: []. Measured, one lane per machine kind: goal encoder on CPU int8 (6.615 ms) overlapping the obs encoder on DSP (9.533 ms), then the transformer on CPU fp32 (13.559 ms) = 23.955 ms makespan, against 29.379 ms for the shipped two-tile set. The extra dispatch the split costs is exactly what the overhead model predicts: the same three tiles run end-to-end with no concurrency are 29.764 ms, i.e. +0.385 ms over the two-tile 29.379 ms against a predicted 0.367 ms DSP dispatch + 5.4 ns x 512 boundary bytes. So the split pays for itself 15x over. The decoder's op range is not a single span because ops 0-5 and 1070 are constant subgraphs shared by every tile that needs them. UPDATE: the decoder is now two tiles. Cutting the 8-op waypoint tail and rewriting the 4 fused GELUs as x*Sigmoid(1.702x) unblocks the DSP (measured 7003.4 us int8, 5 repeats, median; the distribution is wide -- 6096-7858 -- so treat it as +-12%) against 11623.0 us for the same body on CPU fp32. The Conv1x1 step from VINT_FINDINGS.md is deliberately NOT applied: over 5 repeats it measured 7535.9 us on DSP, i.e. no better than without it, while raising waypoint error from 1.48% to 1.72%.

_provenance.statistic: median of per-sweep median_us, performance governor, CPU cells unmasked
_provenance.op_index_space: flow_c IR (605 ops, pytorch_export:vint) -- derived by qnn_models/slicing_study/ir_branch_ranges.py, the same backward-closure partition the ONNX slicer runs, applied to the IR's depends_on edges. The two encoders have NO shared ancestor in IR space, so the partition is exactly ops 0-295 / 296-538 / 539-604. Each binding also carries _ops_onnx_nodes, the node ranges of the ONNX the artifacts were actually sliced from (1931 nodes); the two spaces differ, as they do for yolov8n.

bindings.name: vint_dec_body

compose_blocked.hta@int8: QnnHtaHTA op Reshape supports only equal Input and Output dimensions

bindings._role: the decoder minus its waypoint-integration tail. Splitting at /action_predictor/action_predictor.0/Gemm_output_0 removes the CumulativeSum and both ScatterNd, and rewriting the 4 fused GELUs as x*Sigmoid(1.702x) removes the 'Param[0] has incorrect Value 1' rejection recorded below -- together those are what let this tile compose on the DSP at all.

bindings.name: vint_dec_tail
bindings._role: the [1,20] waypoint integration: 2 StridedSlice, 2 ScatterNd, 1 Reshape, 1 L2Norm, 1 CumulativeSum. CPU-only on purpose -- CumulativeSum and ScatterNd are what blocked the whole decoder from the DSP, and at 74.7 us it is not worth carving further.

_gpu_merge_note: Branch-parallel encoders from the slicing study, plus the GPU option for the decoder measured separately (16.4 ms fp16, 0.96x of cell in a real run, on silicon nothing else uses). The study's own trace had the decoder on the contended CPU at 28.5 ms — 2.05x its cell — so the two results compose: overlap the encoders AND take the decoder off the CPU.
lowering_note: dec_body_g.onnx carries an offline GELU rewrite: the 4 exact (erf) GELUs are re-expressed as x*Sigmoid(1.702x). The v66 DSP rejects a fused GELU with 'Param[0] has incorrect Value 1.' (ElementWiseNeuron operation 1), and those 4 sites were the only thing keeping the decoder off the DSP. Cost: 0.35% of the waypoint output range. Only the decoder tiles carry it; the encoders are unmodified.
